summary: Handle `extends null`, whose prototype topology and construction behavior cannot be represented by ordinary C# inheritance.

target.notes: Construct the JavaScript class/prototype objects with a null prototype for the instance prototype chain and apply JavaScript derived-constructor rules.

semantics.default_constructor: attempts super(...args) and cannot normally construct because null is not a constructor

caveats: Mapping this to `System.Object` changes the JavaScript prototype chain and construction semantics.

tests.name: prototype chain terminates at null
tests.input: class C extends null { constructor(){ return Object.create(null); } } const x=new C(); console.log(Object.getPrototypeOf(C.prototype)===null);

tests.name: edge: default constructor fails
tests.input: class C extends null {} new C();
tests.expected_behavior: throws TypeError because the implicit derived constructor attempts to call null as super
